```python import pytest from jinja2 import Environment from jinja2 import UndefinedError from jinja2 import DictLoader def test_issue_1253_elif_undefined_error(env): template_string = """ {% if new_data_set_created is defined %} {% if new_data_set_created == True %} The new image data set {{ form_data["data_set_name"] }} has been created. {% set form_data = {"data_set_name": "", "client": "", "project": ""} %} {% else %} The new image data set {{ form_data["data_set_name"] }} could not be created.
{% endif %} {% elif deleted_data_set is defined %} The image data set {{ deleted_data_set }} has been deleted from DB and from disk. {% set form_data = {"data_set_name": "", "client": "", "project": ""} %} {% else %} {% set form_data = {"data_set_name": "", "client": "", "project": ""} %} {% endif %} """ env.loader = DictLoader({"image-data-sets.html": template_string}) template = env.get_template("image-data-sets.html") # This call should raise an UndefinedError because form_data is not passed # when new_data_set_created is not defined, and the elif branch is taken. # The bug is that the `elif` branch causes `form_data` to be undefined # in the `else` block of the outer if, even if it's defined in the context. with pytest.raises(UndefinedError) as excinfo: template.render(deleted_data_set="test_dataset") assert "'form_data' is undefined" in str(excinfo.value) # This call should work without error, as form_data is provided and # new_data_set_created is True, so the first branch is taken. # This is to confirm that the template works when form_data is explicitly # used in the first branch. result = template.render(new_data_set_created=True, form_data={"data_set_name": "test_name"}) assert "The new image data set test_name has been created." in result # This call should also work without error, as form_data is provided and # new_data_set_created is False, so the second branch of the inner if is taken. result = template.render(new_data_set_created=False, form_data={"data_set_name": "test_name"}) assert "The new image data set test_name could not be created." in result # This call should work without error, as form_data is provided and # new_data_set_created is not defined, but the else branch is taken, # where form_data is set. result = template.render(form_data={"data_set_name": "initial_name"}) assert "" in result # The else branch just sets form_data, produces no output ```
